Samegrelo:
Don't get trapped on a sanitized tourist bus when you could be exploring the lush, untamed jungles of Samegrelo. This is a fertile, rolling land where the clearest rivers in Georgia rush down from rugged slopes on their way to the sea. You will leave the paved roads behind to discover towering waterfalls, isolated mountain lakes, and quiet beaches that the mainstream crowds ignore.

The Megrelian people speak their own language and live with an infectious, epicurean enthusiasm. While most tourists eat overpriced, mediocre food in the center of town, you will end your days around village tables piled high with feasts. Megrelian food is lavishly flavored with the real, raw spices of their gardens, featuring dishes you simply cannot find anywhere else.

The landscape here is broad and diverse, waiting for you to get your boots muddy. You can navigate a rowboat through the massive, pristine swamps of the Kolkheti Reserve where water buffaloes bathe lazily by the seaside. If you crave a genuine physical challenge, you will hike for days up to the isolated Tobavarchkhili Lake, an alpine secret tucked away in the clouds.

I know the hidden secrets of this region because I have driven the dirt roads and walked the forgotten trails. You will explore the crystal clear waters of Balda Canyon, uncover the ancient Byzantine frescoes of Tsalenjikha, and soak in the outdoor hot springs of Nokalakevi. Tell me what kind of adventure you are looking for, and we will hit the dirt to experience the true character of Samegrelo.
Guria:
Most tourists just drive straight through Guria on their way to crowded seacoast resorts, missing out on one of the most charming parts of Georgia. Their loss is your gain. Nestled in the foothills of the Lesser Caucasus, this small, cozy region offers a genuine connection to the local culture. You will avoid the sterile tourist traps and step directly into a world of sharp humor, yodeling folk songs, and incredibly warm hospitality.

The subtropical climate here is perfect for growing mandarins, guavas, and unique varieties of grapes. Instead of rushing through a scripted itinerary, you will walk or cycle through peaceful villages and explore small medieval churches like Shemokmedi and Jikheti. When the heat rises, you can escape with childlike fun at local river swimming holes known only to the locals.

For those willing to embrace a little grit, the forested foothills and high mountains to the south offer a completely different reality. You will leave the overbuilt resorts behind and venture into the rolling green peaks where summer herding families manufacture cheese amidst endless wildflower fields. This is the raw, unpolished side of the country that you came to experience.

Guria also produces some of the finest tea west of China, including a fermented mountain blueberry leaf tea that you will never forget. I have put the miles in to find these authentic experiences so you do not have to guess where the real Georgia hides. Grab your boots, and we will uncover the rugged, off-road beauty of Guria together.
Adjara:
The Adjarian seacoast is heavily overrun by the sanitized tourism industry, filled with concrete skyscrapers, overpriced restaurants, and cynical seaside traps. Fortunately, you do not have to settle for that manufactured experience. Just a few steps away from the noise, you will discover the real Adjara: a land of steep, jungle-covered mountains, ancient fortresses, and swift rivers carving up the landscape.

The true character of Adjara is found high in the mountains, not on the crowded beaches. You will get your boots muddy navigating steep valleys and crossing medieval stone bridges to reach isolated highland villages. The people here are the most openhearted hosts in all of Georgia, ready to welcome you with a tiny cup of perfectly brewed coffee and a genuine smile.

Highland Adjarians are masterful cheesemakers and beekeepers, taking vast herds of cattle up to the alpine zones every summer. While other travelers eat generic buffet food, you will sit around tables piled high with feasts of kaymagh creams, yagh butter, and tenili string cheese. You will taste mountain floral honey and strong brews of blueberry leaf tea that showcase the abundant, raw flavor of the land.

I know how to navigate the chaos of the coast to bring you safely into these intensely green forests and rolling summer mountains. Whether you want to hike through the Mtirala reserves or join herding families in their wooden cottages, you will experience a Georgia most people never see. Tell me what kind of untamed adventure you want, and we will leave the tourist bubble far behind.
Lechkhumi:
Lechkhumi is the smallest of the Georgian regions, so obscure that even many locals forget it exists. This means you can completely avoid the sanitized tourism industry and step into an untouched, rugged paradise. Enclosed by towering mountains on all sides, this region is a labyrinth of mists, sheer cliffs, and chestnut forests where you will feel the profound, raw reality of the landscape.

At the center of it all rises Khvamli, a massive limestone cliff wrapped in ancient mysteries and millennia-old mythology. You will leave the paved routes behind to discover hidden caves carved with astrological symbols and take in sweeping views of the Black Sea and Mount Elbrus. This is not a polished museum exhibit; it is a visceral encounter with history that you have to earn with your own muddy boots.

For those who crave real adventure, the steep and forbidding Lechkhumi Ridge offers narrow, trackless trails and desolate beauty. You will journey up to Akhalchala, a rustic summer village set in a large meadow surrounded by the region's highest peaks. Up here, you will breathe pure air, drink from clear mountain streams, and experience the majestic isolation that only the truly untamed corners of the world can provide.

Lechkhumi also happens to grow some of the rarest and most delicious grapes in the country, carefully cultivated in small village vineyards. Instead of attending a corporate wine tasting, you will share unpretentious, unforgettable vintages with local families who drink far better than anyone in a fancy boutique. I have explored these obscure pathways for years, and I am ready to guide you straight into the hidden secrets of Lechkhumi.
Racha:
Racha shares the spectacular Rioni river valley with its twin region, Lechkhumi, offering a deeply authentic alternative to crowded tourist hotspots. You will not find any sanitized package tours here. Instead, you will find a slow-paced, rugged landscape where the river flows wild and swift near its birthplace in the high mountains, inviting you to experience the real, unhurried rhythm of village life.

While others rush from one famous landmark to the next, you will take the time to explore the quiet grandeur of Racha's historical sites. You will stand before the intricate stone carvings of Nikortsminda and the isolated beauty of Mravaldzali, staring the Great Caucasus mountains face to face. These are places of deep, grounded history that you can only truly appreciate when you leave the busy highways behind.

The high mountains of Upper Racha are an absolute paradise for those willing to put in the physical effort. You will hike through exquisite pine forests, navigate the forgotten wilderness of Chutkharo, and camp by the pristine, isolated waters of Udziro Lake. This is an environment that demands respect and rewards you with raw, unfiltered panoramas of the Greater Caucasus.

I have spent some of my happiest days wandering these valleys, learning the hidden secrets of the karstic caves and towering waterfalls. My job is to navigate the logistics so you can simply focus on the dirt under your feet and the incredible scale of the mountains above. Jump in the off-road car, and we will find the cozy, untamed adventures waiting in Racha.
Imereti:
Imereti is a sprawling, decadent land that encompasses dense forests, stark canyons, and fertile plains. Do not settle for the standard day trips that trap travelers in a sanitized bubble. You need to venture off the beaten track to experience the true character of this region, from the subterranean rivers of its limestone caves to the spectacular mountain panoramas of the Lesser Caucasus.

The locals here possess a goofy humor and an intense dedication to indulgent gastronomy. While the tourist masses eat generic hotel meals, you will sit around tables piled high with feasts of spiced bean soup, fresh cheese pastries, and wild foraged blackberries. This is authentic, unpretentious hospitality where the food is deeply rooted in the agricultural reality of the Colchian plain.

The landscape demands to be explored with muddy boots and a healthy sense of curiosity. You will hike through the mystical Rioni valley, explore the natural caverns of Tsutskhvati, and discover the forgotten waterfalls of the Khani valley. Whether you are navigating the winding plateau around Chiatura or climbing to the roof of the region at Zekari pass, you will witness the raw, unfettered beauty of the land.

I know the hidden secrets of Imereti because I have actually put the miles in to find them. This province rewards those who are willing to embrace a little grit and leave the guidebook behind. Tell me what kind of untamed adventure you are looking for, and we will hit the dirt to uncover everything Imereti has to offer.
Meskheti:
Meskheti is a stark, dramatic landscape defined by the mighty Mtkvari canyon and the heavy, lingering presence of the Middle Ages. Most tourists hurry out and back on sterile day trips just to snap a photo of the Vardzia cave town before rushing back to the city. We will bypass that artificial rush, leaving the crowds behind to explore the massive, forgotten fortresses and ancient tunnels scattered across the desolate plateaus.

This is a region where the history is as rugged as the terrain itself. You will hike up to the ruins of Tmogvi Castle, stand before the ancient Saro Megaliths, and discover the tangled roots of a 400-year-old grapevine hidden deep in the valley. There are no velvet ropes here; you will experience the visceral reality of medieval architecture slowly being reclaimed by the untamed environment.

Beyond the canyon, the misty ridges of the Tori mountains offer an intense, isolated hiking experience where you will rarely meet another traveler. You will track through forgotten forests to find unmarked hot springs and the alien-like Stone Man of Uraveli, one of the last surviving pagan idols in the country. This is real exploration, where every discovery feels earned by the sweat on your brow.

I have driven these open steppes and navigated these rocky paths to uncover the true character of Meskheti. When you travel with me, you will eat unique local noodles in authentic village guesthouses and sleep under the vast, open sky. Grab your boots, and we will dive into the thrilling, ancient mysteries that this landscape holds.
Javakheti:
The Javakheti Plateau is a vast, volcanic expanse defined by extreme elevations and a profound sense of emptiness. You will not find soft, sanitized comforts here; this is a rugged, hardscrabble environment that demands respect. You will leave the comfortable tourist bubble to experience a land born of fire, where dormant calderas and sprawling alpine lakes dominate the desolate, untamed horizon.

The massive lakes of Javakheti are central to life on the plateau, swarming with migratory birds in the summer and freezing inches thick in the harsh winters. You will meet the resilient ethnic Armenians and pacifist Russian Doukhobors who make their living raising potatoes and fishing in these cold waters. This is a rare opportunity to connect with isolated communities that survive on the very edge of the known world.

For those who want to push their limits, the volcanic peaks offer an otherworldly hiking experience over basalt, obsidian, and pumice. You will climb to heights over 3,300 meters, stepping over ancient stones to reach the monumental Bronze Age megaliths of Abuli and Shaori. These impossible, mortarless structures were built at extreme elevations, offering a visceral connection to a powerful and completely forgotten civilization.

I know the hidden secrets of this plateau because I have spent the time exploring its freezing winds and trackless slopes. My job is to handle the harsh logistics so you can safely experience the majestic isolation and ancient mysteries of Javakheti. Tell me what kind of raw adventure you are seeking, and we will hit the dirt.
Kartli:
Kartli is the historical heartland of Georgia, heavily bypassed by tourists who only stop for a macabre museum tour before fleeing to the next generic landmark. You will avoid that superficial trap and dive straight into the most diverse, historically dense region in the country. We will navigate the vast labyrinth of the Trialeti Range, uncovering forgotten villages and ancient monuments hidden deep in the forests.

The southern marchlands are a raw patchwork of cultures where you will discover the ruined glory of the Georgian Golden Age. You will explore the massive archaeological site of Samshvilde, a city inhabited for six thousand years, and track through dense overgrowth to find abandoned Armenian monasteries and half-timbered German ruins. This is a place where history is not cordoned off behind glass; it is weathered, overgrown, and waiting to be found.

On the quiet Tsalka plateau, you will walk among prehistoric standing stones, dolmens, and the remnants of megalithic fortresses. For a true physical adventure, you will hike the steep ridges of the Algeti and Tedzami valleys, passing by old bandit fortresses and peculiarly decorated ancient chapels. The landscape here is fiercely beautiful, demanding that you get your boots muddy to see the best panoramic views.

I have driven the off-road trails and hiked the steep canyons of Kartli to map out its most authentic experiences. Whether you are exploring the dramatic cliffs of the Ateni valley or sitting down with locals in a remote agricultural village, you will experience a Georgia most people never see. Leave the paved routes behind, and let us uncover the true character of the heartland.
Svaneti:
Svaneti was once a fiercely remote, mountainous stronghold, but today its main towns are rapidly being swallowed by the sanitized tourism industry. You do not have to settle for the concrete hotels and crowded bars that plague the popular centers. Instead, you will venture beyond the tourist traps to experience the raw, towering peaks and the chillingly beautiful traditions that define the true character of this region.

This is a paradise for those who want to test their endurance against the landscape. You will hike steep, narrow trails that connect isolated villages, passing centuries-old defensive stone towers that still guard the valleys. The mountains here dictate the terms of your journey, rewarding your physical effort with visceral, unfiltered views of the Greater Caucasus.

The Svans have a deep, complex history, preserving a culture where Christianity and paganism exist together at ancient stone shrines. You will step inside small, forgotten village churches to witness utterly unique medieval frescoes that survived because of the region's historical isolation. This is an environment that feels like a spiritual gateway to a different world, far removed from the sterile tours of the lowlands.

I know how to navigate the logistical chaos of modern Svaneti to get you safely out into the untamed wilderness. You will leave the crowds behind, eat real food with local families, and get your boots muddy on the high trails. Tell me how deep into the mountains you want to go, and we will find the hidden secrets of Svaneti together.
Mtianeti:
Mtianeti is a vast, forbidding land of undulating ridges, fierce rivers, and massive peaks that loom overhead and distort your sense of scale. You will not find any sanitized comforts here; the grip of winter holds these valleys for more than half the year. When you travel into this region, you are entering a rugged world where the landscape dictates the terms and the ancient mountaineer traditions still hold strong.

This is not a place for casual sightseeing from the window of an air-conditioned bus. You will hike up steep valleys to places like Khevsureti and Tusheti, where ancient defensive towers spring from the green ridges. The mountaineers who live here are sober, serious folk who maintain stone shrines where old pagan customs flow together with Christian traditions in the shadow of the peaks.

When the brief summer arrives and the high pastures bloom with rhododendrons, you will experience the kind of isolation that sets the mind free. You will trek for days out of the sight of civilization, sleeping in tents or sharing rustic shelter with local herders. Whether you are crossing the Datvisjvari Pass or navigating the rushing rivers of Gudamakari, every step must be earned.

I have spent years exploring these endless, fascinating valleys, and I still feel like there is always another secret waiting over the next ridge. My job is to handle the off-road driving and the tough logistics so you can fully immerse yourself in the raw reality of the mountains. Grab your boots, and we will discover the true, unyielding character of Mtianeti.
Kakheti:
Kakheti is heavily marketed as a generic wine region, filled with massive corporate vineyards and kitschily reconstructed fortress towns built to appease the sanitized tourism industry. We will bypass those manufactured experiences entirely. Instead, you will hit the dirt roads to discover the wild, untamed nature and the deeply authentic local culture that the big tour companies actively ignore.

The landscape of Kakheti is shockingly diverse, waiting for you to get your boots muddy. You will hike the green, misty ridges of the Gombori Range and push through the dense, tropical forests of the Greater Caucasus to reach isolated alpine lakes. In the south, you will explore the harsh, dry canyons of the Vashlovani desert, experiencing a profound silence and vast spaces entirely devoid of human traces.

The history here is etched directly into the rugged environment. You will climb up to ancient cave monasteries carved by hand into the desert cliffs, where vibrant medieval frescoes still cling to the rock faces. You will wander through forgotten forests to find slowly toppling, moss-covered basilicas that offer a visceral connection to the past, far away from any velvet ropes or ticket booths.

The true soul of Kakheti is found around tables piled high with feasts, not in sterile tasting rooms. You will share powerful, uniquely funky wines fermented in traditional clay qvevris and eat barbecue roasted over open fires by unpretentious locals. I know the hidden secrets of this massive region, and I am ready to help you experience the raw, unfiltered reality of Kakheti.
Tbilisi:
Tbilisi is a chaotic, beautiful collision of ancient history and modern construction, where soulless concrete skyscrapers constantly threaten to pave over the city's bohemian soul. You will avoid the sterilized, scripted tourist circuits that try to hide the grit. Instead, you will step onto the broken sidewalks to experience the scintillating energy of a true crossroads city built into a dramatic canyon.

The real character of Tbilisi is found in its swarming, serpentine bazaars and its quiet, angular backstreet courtyards. You will leave the main avenues to discover hidden rivers, echoing bathhouses, and subterranean khinkali dungeons where the locals actually spend their time. Every street here heaves with the memories of the Silk Road, offering chance encounters and raw, unscripted nights that you will never forget.

For those who want to dig deeper into the urban fabric, the outskirts of the city hold their own untamed adventures. You will explore the abandoned Soviet factories scattered throughout the outer suburbs or hike up to the ruins of Kojori fortress for spectacular views of the valley. This is not a polished museum city; it is a living, breathing labyrinth that demands to be explored on foot.

While I usually focus on the wild regions beyond the city limits, I know the hidden secrets of my adopted hometown better than anyone. My job is to point you toward the authentic, unpretentious corners of Tbilisi that you will not find in any glossy guidebook. Tell me what kind of urban adventure you are looking for, and we will hit the streets to find the real city.
